**Structure of Matter**

### 3.5.2 Mass Number

The mass number of an atom is denoted by the total number of protons and neutrons in its nucleus. The mass number is expressed by A. Since the mass number is the summation of neutrons and protons, we can get the number of neutrons in an atom by deducing its proton number from the mass number. The mass number of Sodium (Na) is 23, its proton number is 11; so the number of neutrons in sodium is (23 - 11) = 12.

The atomic number of an atom is written at the lower left corner of its symbol while its mass number is written at the upper left corner. In the case with Sodium (Na), it will be written as

**Mass Number (A)**

**Atomic Number/Proton Number (Z)**
